science_trust.label: Grounded in Science
science_trust.subtitle: Our pedagogy is grounded in peer-reviewed neuroscience, developmental cognitive psychology, and randomized controlled trials.
science_trust.card_1_desc: Research proves rhythm perception—not melody—directly mediates reading ability through phonological awareness and auditory memory (Sousa et al.).
science_trust.card_2_desc: Over 1 million genomes analyzed reveal deep genetic links between musical rhythm ability, language processing, and dyslexia risk (the DLAT gene).
science_trust.card_3_desc: A 20-week randomized controlled trial showed that 10 minutes of daily musical rhythm training produced phonological awareness gains equal to dedicated phonics training.
science_trust.card_4_desc: The auditory cortex is most plastic before age 7. Multi-sensory rhythmic learning wires durable neural pathways before reading difficulties emerge.

faq.label: Still Curious?
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about the free Deluxe album and the Rhythm Quest ecosystem.
faq.q1: Why is The Sound of Essentials Deluxe completely free?
faq.a1: The original Sound of Essentials was created as a whole-heart gift to families. The Deluxe edition remains free so every child has access to foundational sensory and musical learning. Instant digital access requires only an email, with optional learning materials and physical editions available at checkout.
faq.q2: How do I get instant digital access?
faq.a2: Simply click 'Start the Free Experience' and enter your email. You will immediately receive private streaming access to all 19 tracks, direct audio download links, and the printable 40-page coloring book PDF.
faq.q3: What age group is this designed for?
faq.a3: The Sound of Essentials is designed specifically for children ages 2–7 (Toddler, Pre-K, Kindergarten, 1st & 2nd Grade). It is structured for both home listening and early classroom environments.
faq.q4: How does musical rhythm build reading skills?
faq.a4: Peer-reviewed research in Nature Scientific Reports confirms that rhythm discrimination trains the brain's temporal processing—the exact mechanism used to segment syllables and phonemes when learning to read.
faq.q5: What is The Seven Land Quest ($19)?
faq.a5: The Seven Land Quest is our comprehensive 7-week guided learning companion. It expands the 19 songs into 400 interactive activities, physical movement games, printable adventure maps, and weekly rhythm milestones.

science.hero_subtitle: Chronicles of the Clock: Understanding the neurological architecture behind every rhythm.
science.track_title: Do You Know What Time It Is?
science.beyond_desc_1: It may seem just like lyrics to a catchy song, but dive deeper and you'll see a brilliantly disguised lesson in Temporal Scaffolding and Numeracy.
science.beyond_desc_2: This track is a vital addition to Celestia: The Garden of Time, where our heroes Elias & Selene guide children through abstract concepts.
science.breakdown_subtitle: Every element of the SOE curriculum is designed to support neurological development and executive function.

sequencing.title: Rhythmic Sequencing
sequencing.desc: By distinctly separating whole hours from half-hours, we introduce fractional concepts and sequential logic.

anchoring.title: Anchoring Abstract Concepts
anchoring.desc: Time is invisible and difficult for toddlers to grasp. We solve this by linking abstract numbers to concrete, physical anchors.

regulation.title: Emotional Regulation
regulation.desc: Unpredictability creates anxiety. Mapping the day builds Executive Function.

science.implementation_desc_1: In our "Teacher's Guide" or interactive website, we pair this song with a visual "daily routine chart."
science.implementation_desc_2: Parents and educators point to a clock face during the numbers. This physical "serve and return" interaction durably anchors the learning.
science.rhythm_subtitle: Independent research keeps arriving at the same conclusion. Rhythm is the musical element that prepares young brains to read.

rhythm_not_melody.title: Rhythm, Not Melody
rhythm_not_melody.desc: A 2022 study in Nature Scientific Reports found that rhythm perception, not melody, links musical ability to reading through phonological awareness. Rhythm is our foundation by design.

preschool.title: Proven in Preschool
preschool.desc: In a controlled trial, 10 minutes of daily music training built phonological awareness in preschoolers as effectively as a dedicated phonics program. The window is ages 2 to 7. So is our focus.

genetics.title: Written in Our DNA
genetics.desc: A 2024 study of over one million people found 16 genome regions shared between rhythm ability and language skills. Music and reading grow from the same roots.

science.equity_note: In one study, a single year of music training brought low-income children to age-appropriate reading levels while untrained peers fell behind. This is why we call music essential.
science.beyond2_desc_1: "Slow down and say" is the whole lesson. Each hard word is broken into syllables and carried by the beat. Researchers call this phonological segmentation, and it is one of the strongest predictors of reading success.
science.beyond2_desc_2: This track lives in Luminosity, where our heroes Athena & Ezra turn intimidating words into rhythmic play. A child who can feel the beat of a word is learning to read it.
science.pedagogy_validated: Published research links these group methods to reading achievement in school-age children.
science.references_subtitle: A selection of the peer-reviewed research that informs the SOE method.
science.cta_subtitle: Experience how these neurological principles translate into joyful melody.
